name: Global Solo Banking Access Index
description: Which US business banking providers accept non-US-resident founders of US LLCs — evidence-cited matrix across 19 providers and 8 countries of residence. Every cell carries a source URL, evidence tier, and date; absence of evidence is reported as unknown, never inferred.
methodology: Two-stage pipeline: (1) per-provider evidence mining restricted to fetchable sources with verbatim quotes; (2) independent adversarial verification that re-fetched every source and discarded claims whose quotes were absent, misread, or overreached (239 of 268 mined claims survived). Country cells are tri-state: explicit_accept / explicit_restrict / no_published_restriction — absence from a prohibited list is never converted into acceptance. Two optional discriminators sit alongside that status in the JSON, because a single label was hiding materially different evidence on both sides of it: unknown_kind (four values) says WHY a cell is unknown, and restrict_kind (4 values) says HOW a restriction is evidenced — 8 cells name the country on a published prohibited list, 2 name it with a stated restriction attached, 15 deduce it from a closed eligibility list, and 40 derive it from a blanket citizenship/residency rule that names no country at all. The reader outcome is the same in each; the provenance is not, and this dataset is about the provenance. NOT EVERY FIELD IS IN THAT 239: dimensions added after the adversarial pass are single-pass research and are listed, with the reason, in dimension_provenance below. Read it before citing those fields at the same confidence as the core.

dimension_provenance.receive: The `receive` dimension (field: inbound_international) was added 2026-07-26 (17 claims) and 2026-08-14 (Revolut Business) by single-pass primary-source research. On 2026-10-03 all 18 went through a refute-first adversarial pass by an independent verifier that re-fetched every cited source, with a positive control on each body (record: data/banking-access-index/verification-receive-2026-10-03.json). Result: 8 CONFIRMED as written; 8 CONFIRMED with the value holding but the summary saying more than its page — each summary was cut back to what the page states (e.g. Wise's 'rejects SWIFT payments without the recipient's address', Lili's 'help centre has said 51 countries'); 2 REFUTED AS CITED — Chase's source was the consumer wire FAQ and Revolut's was a marketing page that never mentions SWIFT. Neither value reversed: both were re-sourced to the providers' own business documents (Chase's Business Fee Schedule effective 06/14/2026; two en-US Revolut Business help articles) and confirmed by a second independent verifier. All 18 now carry `verification: adversarial_2026-10-03` and are counted in claim_count (239 → 257). The column is uniformly `swift_supported`; the verifier was told to treat that uniformity as a reason for more suspicion and checked each source on its own. Pattern worth keeping: every overreach was a true value with an enriched summary — detail that came from a neighbouring page or from memory — so the summary, not the value, is where single-pass research drifts.
dimension_provenance.card: The `card` dimension (field: issuance) — the 'account openable ≠ card obtainable' gate: whether physical cards ship internationally and whether virtual cards are issuable to abroad-resident owners — was added 2026-07-28 by single-pass primary-source research (5 parallel research passes, vendor help centers/terms only, verbatim quotes; one Wayback-archived citation at Airwallex flagged for re-verify). Not through the refute-first adversarial pass until 2026-10-27 (below). Re-read 2026-10-04: every evidence quote in this dimension was re-matched against a fresh fetch of its source (scripted match, then every miss re-read against the live page); record data/banking-access-index/reverify-cardphone-2026-10-04.json. This confirms the quotes; it is not an adversarial verification, so the dimension stays single-pass. ADVERSARIAL PASS 2026-10-27: two independent refute-first verifiers re-fetched every cited source for the 18 non-superseded rows, with a positive control on each body; every proposed change was then re-read against the live page by a second reader before it was applied (record: data/banking-access-index/verification-cardphone-2026-10-27.json). Result: 8 CONFIRMED as written; 9 CONFIRMED with the value holding but the summary cut back to its page (e.g. Mercury's tier counts, Payoneer's unstated shipping countries, Rho's uncited virtual-address ban); 1 SOURCE MOVED (Brex: the shipping quote is live again on the card-overview page, and the 13-country courier list flagged as uncited on 2026-08-14 was found in that page's Troubleshooting section). No issuance value changed. One proposed change was rejected: Airwallex to international_shipping on the strength of its Issuing API documentation, a different product surface that speaks of delivery destination, not cardholder residence. The 12 surviving non-unknown cells now count toward claim_count.
dimension_provenance.phone_2fa: The `phone_2fa` dimension (fields: us_phone_required, voip_policy, alt_2fa) — signup phone requirements, published VoIP/virtual-number policies, and published phone-free second factors — was added 2026-07-28 by the same single-pass research as `card`. Notable method rule: voip_policy records `published_blocked` only where the vendor states it verbatim (Wells Fargo, Novo, Bluevine, Lili-standard-flow); silence after a successful help-center search is `no_published_policy`, never converted to acceptance or blocking. Internal vendor contradictions (Relay, Bluevine, Slash) are recorded verbatim in summaries without resolution. Re-read 2026-10-04: every evidence quote in this dimension was re-matched against a fresh fetch of its source (scripted match, then every miss re-read against the live page); record data/banking-access-index/reverify-cardphone-2026-10-04.json. This confirms the quotes; it is not an adversarial verification, so the dimension stays single-pass. One vendor change was applied: Bluevine's MFA article no longer requires a US cellular number, so Bluevine moved to not_required / no_totp. ADVERSARIAL PASS 2026-10-27: two independent refute-first verifiers re-fetched every cited source for 17 non-superseded rows (51 fields) and researched Revolut Business's three fields for the first time; every proposed change was then re-read against the live page by a second reader before it was applied (record: data/banking-access-index/verification-cardphone-2026-10-27.json). Values changed: Payoneer alt_2fa no_totp→totp (its authenticator-app FAQ); Brex voip_policy→published_blocked and us_phone_required→not_required (its phone-number article); us_phone_required not_required→unknown for Mercury, Wise, Payoneer and Airwallex (each rested on silence, not a statement) and required→unknown for Bank of America and Wells Fargo (both publish a non-SMS route; their sources are consumer pages). Rejected: Found alt_2fa sms_only→no_totp — the email code it rested on is a password-reset path, not a second factor. Revolut Business's new values are single-pass and excluded. The surviving non-unknown fields now count toward claim_count.
dimension_provenance.pboc_register: `countries.china.pboc_register` was added 2026-08-11 from a full 158/158 retrieval of the PBoC 已获许可机构（支付机构）register accessed 2026-07-26 (8 list pages + 158 detail pages retained as raw HTML). It is present on the 3 providers the retrieval matched — out of the 18 in the index ON THAT DATE — and is deliberately ABSENT, not 'unknown', on the rest, which are US-domiciled banks and fintechs the register categorically cannot contain; printing a value for them would manufacture a signal out of a wrong-register lookup. PRESENT-DAY SPLIT, corrected 2026-08-27: the index now holds 19 providers, so it is 3 with the field and 16 without. Revolut Business was added as provider #19 on 2026-08-14, AFTER this retrieval, and has never been run against the register — its absence is inherited from the retrieval's date, not from a lookup. The '18' above is kept because it is the true denominator of the pass; do not re-read it as a current provider count. The field asserts a listing as printed on the accessed date, never a live licence: the register carries no status field and 10 of its 158 rows print an already-expired 有效期至. brand→entity linkage is a separate and weaker evidence layer than the register fact and is graded per row. Like the receive/card/phone_2fa dimensions this is single-pass research excluded from claim_count, and it has NOT been through the refute-first adversarial pass that produced the 239-claim core.
dimension_provenance.unknown_kind: `countries.*.unknown_kind` was added 2026-08-14 (S196) as an ADDITIVE discriminator on cells whose `status` is `unknown`. It does not change the `status` enum, which is the public contract carried by the CC-BY exports and the Zenodo release. Motivation: an audit of all 39 unknown cells found they were four materially different states wearing one label, and that 23 of the 39 asserted absence with NO citation at all — recording 'not found' without recording where we looked, which is the failure mode that makes a false negative uncorrectable because it reads like a completed investigation. Values: `no_policy_published` (25) — the provider publishes no country-of-residence policy anywhere we looked; the cited URL is the page such a policy would live on. `mentioned_for_other_purpose` (8) — provider material names the country, but for wire destinations, spend-management support, marketing, or country of incorporation, none of which is founder-residency evidence; recorded so a later pass does not re-mine the mention and mistake it for acceptance. `absent_from_non_exhaustive_list` (5, all Bluevine) — a SUPPORTED-country list exists and is explicitly non-exhaustive ('including'), so absence from it carries no information either way; this differs from `no_published_restriction`, where a PROHIBITED list exists and absence means not-prohibited. `conflicting_sources` (1, Meow/Nigeria) — two live provider pages disagree and no single published verdict exists. This is not an absence. Evidence added in this pass is dated `accessed 2026-07-08` where the URL is reused from the original mining pass, and `accessed 2026-08-14` only where the page was actually re-read in the S196 session. No `status` value was changed and no claim was added to `claim_count`.
dimension_provenance.single_pass_recheck_2026_08_14: S196 2026-08-14 — CITATION-INTEGRITY PASS over `receive`, `card` and `phone_2fa`. What was done: all 89 evidence URLs behind the 53 claims in these three dimensions were re-probed, and every anomaly the probe surfaced was then chased at content level. What was NOT done: the refute-first adversarial re-verification these dimensions still owe — no claim whose citations resolved cleanly was independently re-argued. `verification` values are therefore unchanged and claim_count is NOT incremented; these dimensions remain a lower evidence tier than the 239-claim core. Results: 77 of 89 URLs live on first probe; 10 returned 403 (Cloudflare/Zendesk challenge at Mercury, Lili, Grasshopper — a 403 is a bot gate, NOT a dead link, and was not recorded as one); 1 Wayback URL rate-limited (498); 1 found.com timeout that returned 200 on retry and is recorded as transient rather than as a finding. Substantive outcomes: (1) meow.receive was REFUTED by a live vendor page and corrected off `unknown`; (2) brex.card's primary citation was deleted by the vendor and was repaired with a Wayback snapshot carrying the verbatim quote, rather than the value being dropped; (3) airwallex.card was DOWNGRADED to `unknown` because its restriction now survives only in an archive while the live successor article is silent; (4) an uncited sub-claim inside brex.card (a 13-country courier list) was searched for on three pages, not located, and is now flagged in place instead of being silently kept or silently deleted; (5) 12 URLs were migrated to vendor-moved locations (Relay off its support subdomain, Rho to /help-center/, three retitled articles); (6) NorthOne's two claims were CONFIRMED — both assert that every NorthOne surface redirects to Relay, and both redirects still behave exactly that way. The general lesson this pass re-earns: a citation rots before the claim does, and the repair is to restore a source, not to delete a value.
dimension_provenance.revolut_business_addition: Revolut Business was added as provider #19 on 2026-08-14 (S196) by single-pass primary-source research across four vendor pages, all read in that session. It has NOT been through the refute-first adversarial re-verification pass, so its claims are EXCLUDED from claim_count, which stays at 239 and continues to describe only the adversarially verified core. UPDATE 2026-10-03: its `receive` claim has since passed the adversarial pass (re-sourced, see dimension_provenance.receive) and is counted; its other claims are still single-pass and still excluded. Origin: the S196 affiliate ICP screen declined a Revolut affiliate application because GS could not answer 'which ICP subset does this serve' — Revolut was absent from this index and its only appearance anywhere in GS data was inside a quoted Stripe passage. Researching it to dataset standard was the evidence-first alternative to applying blind, and it resolved the question: Revolut Business does admit non-US-resident owners of US entities, but only from a closed list of countries of residence. Two of the row's cells are deliberately left open rather than guessed — `rails` because two published statements conflict (local account details and ACH versus a prepaid-card banking disclosure), and `phone_2fa` because it was not researched at all, which the cell says in as many words so it is not mistaken for a searched-and-empty result. UPDATE 2026-10-27: the rest of the row passed the refute-first adversarial pass (record: data/banking-access-index/verification-cardphone-2026-10-27.json) and joins claim_count — 13 claims, see claim_count_note. `rails` now carries the Business Terms' prepaid-card statement but keeps rails_type unknown, since the custody structure is still unpublished; `phone_2fa` was researched for the first time and stays single-pass until it is re-argued.

evidence_tiers.T1: Provider official documentation (help center, terms, published country lists)
evidence_tiers.T1-archived: A T1 page read from an Internet Archive copy because the live page moved or was removed
evidence_tiers.T2: Provider blog posts or official support statements
evidence_tiers.T3: Dated user reports (forum/Reddit permalinks), unverified by provider

access_score_method: Each provider carries access_score, two figures that are always read as a pair and never averaged. access_openness = 100 × (explicit_accept − explicit_restrict) / 8 over the country cells; no_published_restriction and unknown both count 0, so silence is never read as acceptance. evidence_coverage = round(100 × evidence_credit / evidence_cells), where evidence_cells = 8 countries + 9 dimension blocks (entity, residency, rails, receive, card, phone_2fa, fdic, onboarding, marketplace) and each cell earns its best evidence tier: T1 = 1, T1-archived = 1, T2 = 0.5, no evidence with a URL (or a missing block) = 0. A documented search that found nothing counts as evidence. No weights are chosen; the figures are counts, recomputable from this file. They do not rank providers.

entity.summary: Requires a company formed and registered in the US or a US territory with existing or planned US operations; foreign-owned US companies supported. Money services businesses and crypto exchanges, adult entertainment, cannabis, internet gambling, and trusts excluded — though the same page states Mercury does support many other crypto and Web3 businesses, including startups, DAOs and funds.

residency.summary: No US citizenship or residency required to apply, per provider's help center; international applicants may provide a passport as ID; SSN/ITIN not listed among required application documents.

rails.summary: Demand deposit accounts with own routing and account numbers at partner banks Choice Financial Group and Column N.A.; customers hold direct contractual agreements with the partner banks.

receive.summary: Accepts inbound international wires in 139 non-USD currencies via both partner banks, auto-converted to USD on arrival — the account cannot hold a non-USD balance. The inbound FX cost depends on which partner bank the account sits at: Mercury states Column N.A. "converts incoming funds to USD at the mid-market rate" while Choice Financial Group "uses third-party intermediary banks that typically add a 2-3% markup to the exchange rate." Choice accounts additionally require the sender to populate Remittance Information (Section 70) or the wire may be delayed or returned.

evidence.quote: Customers on either of our partner banks, Choice Financial Group or Column N.A., Members FDIC, can accept international wires in non-USD currencies. In both cases, the funds are automatically converted to USD before they hit your account. Column N.A. converts incoming funds to USD at the mid-market rate. Choice Financial Group uses third-party intermediary banks that typically add a 2-3% markup to the exchange rate.

card.summary: Mercury publishes two lists. Tier 1 (incl. Nigeria, Vietnam, Russia): it will not mail physical cards or issue virtual cards to residents. Tier 2 (incl. China, India, Pakistan, Indonesia, Philippines, Nepal, Sri Lanka): it will not mail physical cards; the page does not list virtual cards as restricted for these. International cards ship via Deutsche Post, typically 2-3 weeks. The page also says shipments to Bahrain, Israel, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the UAE are paused, and suggests creating a virtual card meanwhile.

evidence.quote: We are unable to mail physical cards or issue virtual cards to users who reside in the following countries: [31-country list incl. Nigeria] ... We are also unable to mail physical cards to the following countries: [15-country list incl. China, India, Pakistan] ... In the meantime, you can create a virtual card and begin using it right away.
Cards are shipped via USPS (for U.S. addresses) or Deutsche Post (for international addresses) ... International addresses: Typically arrive in 2-3 weeks

phone_2fa.summary: 2FA methods published: authenticator app (TOTP), security key, or passkey; the 2FA article lists no SMS option and calls TOTP codes more secure than SMS-based codes. Whether a US phone number is needed is not published: the application-requirements checklist lists no phone number of any kind, and that silence is recorded as unknown, not read as acceptance of a non-US number. No published VoIP/virtual-number policy found (help-center searches for 'phone number' and 'SMS two-factor' plus full reads of the 2FA and eligibility articles).

caveats: Country entries marked 'no published restriction' reflect absence from Mercury's prohibited-countries list only; Mercury states eligibility is determined following a full review of each application, and no page affirms acceptance for any specific residence country.

The list runs to 48 countries plus 4 sanctioned regions and reaches well past the eight columned in this index; it is scoped to where a founder LIVES, not to citizenship. A reader whose country has no column here learns nothing from that absence — read the linked list. Named on it and not columned: Indonesia, the Philippines, Vietnam, Bangladesh, Nepal, Venezuela and Angola, and — against the assumption that Europe is safe — Albania, Croatia and Latvia, the last two EU member states (verified against the list 2026-07-15).
Mercury's published residence restrictions are stated for founders and financial controllers; no published statement addresses a passive 25%+ beneficial owner resident in a prohibited country.
Registered agent addresses, P.O. boxes, and UPS Store addresses are not accepted for the company's principal place of business; residential addresses are accepted.

Partner-bank structure is in transition: OCC conditional approval (April 2026) for Mercury's own bank charter is pending, and one FAQ section still names former partner Evolve Bank & Trust; the FDIC entry reflects the Choice/Column structure as of 2026-07-08.

No published statement addresses video-KYC or personal proof-of-address requirements for individual owners; the remote-onboarding entry rests on the provider's statement that physical US presence is not required.

rails.summary: Revolut's US Business Terms (version dated January 22, 2026) settle the question this cell used to leave open: "Your account is associated with a business prepaid card issued by Lead Bank", and the funds "on deposit in your Revolut Business Card are held by Lead Bank" (FDIC-insured to applicable limits if deposit-insurance requirements are met). Revolut does not use the words pooled, FBO or virtual, so the exact custody structure is not published in the pages read, and the rails type stays unknown rather than being collapsed to 'virtual / collection account'. That custody structure is what decides whether a payer's verification, a lender, or a government portal will accept the account details.
